summary: Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor in the root-texts department at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1977 and 1990–1998.

Semën Gesselevič Rudin (1929–1973) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1947 to 1952, earning his Kand. filol. nauk around 1968. He held a post at Saint Petersburg State University in 1955.
Sen Wang (1912–1991) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University from circa 1932 to 1935 and later served as a professor at Minzu University of China.

Senarat Wijayasundara specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Senarath Paranavitana (1896–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean Philippe Vogel and held a post at Leiden University from circa 1934 to 1936, succeeding Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe.

Senchu Murano (b. 1908) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Rissho University by 1933 and the University of Washington by 1938. He later served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Sengaku Mayeda (1931–2026) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under W. Norman Brown at UPenn. He taught at UPenn, the University of Tokyo (1973; emeritus 1982–1991), and Musashino University (~1991–2001).

Senkyo Sakawa (b. 1937) is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Rissho University (completing studies in 1965). He served there as a professor of Buddhism (attested 1981–1985) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Senmyo Naniwa (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under P. V. Bapat, M. G. Dhadphale, and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Bukkyo University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2005).
Sensho Kimura (b. 1943) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor, attested in 2000.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani and Toyo universities. He held lectureships at Komazawa and Otani, directed schools, and served as lecturer (1888) and professor (1917–1923) at the University of Tokyo.

Seok-hyeong Kim (b. 1904) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University, he served as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Attested in 2026, he serves as Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University.

Seongjoon Cheong works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. from Dongguk University (1995–1999). He was a research fellow at the Translation Institute of Tibetan Buddhist Canon (2015–2016) and a research professor at Uiduk University (2023–2024).

Seraphim Rose (1934–1982) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Alan Watts and attended USC, CIIS, and UC Berkeley. He later held a post with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergej Konstantinovich Bulich (1859–1921) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kazan State University under Baudouin de Courtenay and Kruszewski, and abroad in Berlin, Jena, and Leipzig, later becoming professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Saint Petersburg State University in 1891.

Sergey Burmistrov is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed a D.Sci. at Saint Petersburg State University. He held assistant professorships at Saint Petersburg State University (2003–2011) and became a leading researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 2011.

Sergey Malov (1880–1957) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and Saint Petersburg State University, later holding posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1917–1957) and the Institute of Linguistics (1934–1957).

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minaev. He became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University, permanent secretary of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum.

Sergiu Anatol Al-George (1922–1981) was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied under Mircea Eliade. He earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and the University of Delhi, and taught at the University of Bucharest from 1971 to 1973.
